reasoning_traces.think:
The Rollcast framework constructs probabilistic forecasts by combining a set of rolling statistical anchors—mean, median, extrema, regression endpoint, and quantiles—into a weighted mixture. Each anchor is assigned a responsibility based on its proximity to the current state, computed via a softmax function over distance metrics. The weights are then used to form a predictive distribution that adapts to local data characteristics. A key innovation is the state-adaptive persistence gate, which dynamically adjusts how much past information influences the current forecast. This gate is defined by an exponential decay function of state movement, ensuring that when the system is stable, it retains more memory, but when shocks occur, it quickly adapts. The method avoids global modeling by relying solely on local anchor behavior and residual archives. It is evaluated synthetically against oracle DGPs, showing strong performance in terms of coverage and CRPS, though synthetic-only evaluation prevents adoption without real-world validation.
